gloss: renewal fee (especially on a rental contract)

definitions.gloss: renewal fee (especially on a rental contract)
definitions.explanation: A fee paid when renewing a contract — most often an apartment lease, but also driver's licenses, domain names, and memberships. In the context of rental housing, the term specifically refers to a lump-sum payment (typically equivalent to one to two months' rent) paid to the landlord every two years.

examples.japanese: {更新料|こうしんりょう}を{払|はら}う。
{家賃|やちん}の{更新料|こうしんりょう}は{一|いっ}ヶ{月分|げつぶん}です。
examples.english: The rent renewal fee is equivalent to one month's rent.

examples.japanese: {更新料|こうしんりょう}の{負担|ふたん}が{大|おお}きいので、{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しを{検討|けんとう}している。
examples.english: Because the burden of the renewal fee is heavy, I'm considering moving.

notes:
Composed of {更新|こうしん} (renewal, update) and {料|りょう} (fee, charge). In everyday Japanese life, {更新料|こうしんりょう} most often refers to the contract renewal fee on rental apartments, which is a well-known — and frequently grumbled-about — feature of the Japanese housing system. It is typically paid to the landlord once every two years when the lease is renewed, on top of the regular rent.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The practice is common especially in the Kanto area, but much less so in other regions. In some rental contracts (particularly in the Kansai area), there is no {更新料|こうしんりょう} at all, and the tenant instead pays a relatively higher monthly rent or other fees.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {更新料|こうしんりょう}を{払|はら}う: to pay a renewal fee
- {更新料|こうしんりょう}なし: no renewal fee (often used as a selling point in rental listings)
- {家賃|やちん}{一|いっ}ヶ{月分|げつぶん}の{更新料|こうしんりょう}: a renewal fee equal to one month's rent
- {契約|けいやく}{更新|こうしん}{時|じ}の{更新料|こうしんりょう}: renewal fee at contract renewal

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {礼金|れいきん}: "key money" — non-refundable gift to the landlord paid when moving in
- {敷金|しききん}: security deposit — refundable, used to cover damages
- {仲介|ちゅうかい}{手数料|てすうりょう}: broker's commission
- {家賃|やちん}: monthly rent
